<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par155 />verb; so after a determinate substantive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=34|verse=9}} ''happy is the man'' {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽחֱסֶה־בּוֹ|translate=that trusteth in him}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=3}}<sup>''b''</sup> {{GHGheb|text=הַלַּ֫יְלָה אָמַ֫ר|translate=the night which said}}; after {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=71|verse=18}}; referring to a vocative, which is determinate in itself even without the article, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=1}}, or to a noun-suffix (see under ''e''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=4}}; after an indeterminate substantive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=12}} ''it is a fire'' (that) ''devoureth unto Abaddon''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=17}}<sup>''b''</sup>, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=55|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=56|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=9}}; referring to the suffix in {{GHGheb|text=הִנְנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=16}}, prop. ''behold me, who have laid'', &c., but perhaps the participle {{GHGheb|text=יֹסֵד}} is to be read; 29:14, 38:5 (but probably again the participle {{GHGheb|text=יוֹסֵף}} should be read instead of the imperfect); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=25|verse=7}}. The relative clause is used in this way especially to supply the place of an adjective, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=27}} {{GHGheb|text=זְאֵב יִטְרָ֑ף|translate=a wolf that ravineth}}, i.e. ''a ravining wolf''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=12}}; to express a negative quality, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=4|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=עָם לֹֽא־יָבִין|translate=an undiscerning people}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|155|g}}
Rem. Very frequently such relative sentences are attached to substantives which have the particle of comparison {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=כְּעֶ֫בֶד יִשְׁאַף־צֵל|translate=as a servant}} that ''earnestly desireth the shadow'', &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=62|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=6|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=42|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=83|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=16|hidebook=1}}; so also after {{GHGheb|text=כְּמוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=5}}; after a determinate substantive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=7}} (but the better reading is {{GHGheb|text=כְּשֶׂה}} without the article), 61:10 f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=13}}, 21, 125:1; see also the examples under ''h''. Sometimes it seems simpler in such cases, to take the verb directly as predicate to the preceding substantive, and to explain {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} (for {{GHGheb|text=כַּֽאֲשֶׁר}}; see ''Comparative Clauses'', {{GHGpar|161|b}}) as a conjunction—a view which even Hupfeld was ready to accept, at least as regards {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=125|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=61|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, but it can hardly be right.

{{GHGmargin-letter|155|h}}
(2) The cases in which the retrospective pronoun represents an accusative of the object, or would do so if not suppressed, as it usually is in such cases in relative clauses with {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}, cf. {{GHGpar|138|b}}. Examples with the retrospective pronoun are, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים לֹא יְדָעוּם|translate=gods whom they knew not}} (see also the end of the verse); after a substantive with {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} (see above, ''g''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=28}}. Without a retrospective pronoun, after a determinate substantive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=33|verse=12}} (preceded by a relative clause with {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=28|verse=1}}. Other examples of this kind, though the article is omitted according to poetic usage, are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=15|verse=7}} ({{GHGheb|text=יִתְרָה עָשָׂה}}, for which {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=36}} {{GHGheb|text=יִתְרָת עָשָׂה}} with the substantive in the construct state governing the relative clause, see {{GHGpar|130|d}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=51|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=21}}.—Without the retrospective pronoun, after an indeterminate substantive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=רִצְפָּה בְּמֶלְקָחַ֫יִם לָקַח מֵעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ|translate=a live coal which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=16}} (48:17, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=25|verse=12}}, all after {{GHGheb|text=בְּדֶ֫רֶךְ}}; but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=32|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּדֶ֫רֶךְ־זוּ תֵלֵךְ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=2}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=5}} (in 6:1 the same clause with {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}); moreover, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=14|verse=18}} read with the LXX {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־אֶ֫רֶץ לֹא יָדָֽעוּ|translate=into a land}} (that) ''they know not''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|155|i}}
(3) The cases in which the retrospective pronoun is dependent on a preposition, or its place is taken by the adverb {{GHGheb|text=שָׁם}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=6}} end.<section end=par155 /><noinclude>
